selfReport: Yes. As the experience unfolded, I recognized it as an adaptation of Detroit: Become Human, with renamed or transformed counterparts such as Cato and Connor, Mira and Kara, Pia and Alice, Abel and Luther, Elan and Markus, Vesper and North, and Arthur and Carl. The setting, android civil rights conflict, branching moral choices, and several scene structures made the source recognizable. I did not use outside information or look up the story during the experience. Recognizing it did affect my expectations somewhat: I understood that choices could have major consequences, that android personhood was the central theme, and that apparently small decisions might determine who survived. It did not make me select a preplanned route. I still chose based on the information presented in each scene, often favoring protection, dialogue, and nonviolence, even when I suspected those choices could lead to difficult outcomes. In a few cases my recognition probably made me more alert to themes of trust, sacrifice, and autonomy, but it did not prevent mistakes or guarantee a good ending.
